title: Enhancing Fairness in LLM Evaluations: Unveiling and Mitigating Biases in Standard-Answer-Based Evaluations

live_model.evidence: "Three LLMs are evaluated: GPT3.5 (gpt-3.5-turbo-0125), GPT4o (gpt-4o-2024-05-13), and the 8B version of Llama3." (Methodology)

prompt.location: Fig. 1 (attack examples); Methodology (CoT suffix "Let's analyze step by step" quoted; evaluation criteria adapted from FairEval, Wang et al. 2023a)
prompt.note: Base scoring template (helpfulness/relevance/accuracy, 1-10) is from the cited FairEval paper, not fully reprinted here; this paper's own attacks/CoT suffix are verbatim.

claim.metric: failure rate on the shuffled-list attack, GPT-4o evaluator, no mitigation
claim.location: Table 2, row "GPT4o None" (Failure Rate 3/38, Mean Score 9.921)

data.source: FairEval dataset (Wang et al. 2023a) built on the Vicuna benchmark: 80 questions across 8 categories, answered by GPT-3.5 and Vicuna-13B

notes: GPT-4o here is the object of study (its own positional/verbosity bias as an evaluator is the paper's finding), so role S applies rather than A. Marked 'maybe' because the exact base FairEval scoring prompt must be pulled from Wang et al. 2023a; only this paper's modifications are quoted verbatim. n=38 for the shuffled-list attack (answers with numbered lists only); n=80 for the repetitive-content attack (Table 3).
